title: Armstrong seeing himself as an institution
summary: In Macon he said many people had never seen him; Little Rock made him realize his words carried weight.

story.theme_name: Working with and around Louis Armstrong
story.community_name: Playing with and around Louis Armstrong

blocks.x: Yeah, uh, some people have said, Louie's, uh, how did Louie view himself?
Interesting question. Uh, let me, let me tell you this. Yeah. I saw, the time when I saw Louie in Macon, he was not very well. Uh huh.

66, I guess. Yeah, it was in 66, because that was the year the article came out in life. Right. I said to Louie, Louie, you know, you're not looking well and, uh, I mean you're in good enough shape now that you don't need to be playing every night of your life. Exactly. You know, uh, you should only be playing when you feel like playing. And he says to me, he says, Pops, you know how many people in this world have never seen this, you know, Louis Armstrong? In other words, he considered it an obligation. Everybody had.
For everybody to have an opportunity to see him.

And, uh, by that time he had already thought of himself as an institution. Uh huh. And I suspect that that idea came to him relatively late. Uh huh. And probably started at the time when he took a stand on Eisenhower and the Little Rock thing. Uh huh. When he said, uh, that man should go to Little Rock and take those little children by the hand and march him right into school.
Well that was, that was for him. Yeah. That was, uh, we always view Louie as being non-controversial.
Well he was controversial then. But exactly. Yeah. And, uh, he was deliberate about it and he knew it. But he was also impressed by the uproar over it.
Yeah. And he didn't realize that, that anything he said or did would have that kind of influence. Uh huh. And, uh, he was kind of sobered by that. Yeah.

Oh, yeah, I was about to say. Well you probably learned that his words had impact. Yeah, sure. And he didn't realize that he could have that much, that Louie Armstrong carried that much weight. Yeah, he began to see himself as an institution.
